definitions.explanation: Describes a person or manner that tends to hold back, be restrained, or avoid imposing on others. Conveys a habitual tendency toward reserve rather than a single instance.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{遠慮|えんりょ}がちに{手|て}を{挙|あ}げた。
{新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}は{遠慮|えんりょ}がちな{態度|たいど}で{会議|かいぎ}に{出席|しゅっせき}していた。
examples.english: The new employee attended the meeting with a reserved attitude.

examples.japanese: {遠慮|えんりょ}がちな{性格|せいかく}のせいで、{自分|じぶん}の{意見|いけん}をなかなか{言|い}えないことがある。
examples.english: Because of my reserved personality, I sometimes have trouble speaking up with my own opinions.

notes:
USAGE:
The suffix がち indicates a tendency or inclination. Can be used as a な-adjective ({遠慮|えんりょ}がちな{人|ひと}) or adverbially ({遠慮|えんりょ}がちに). The がち suffix attaches to many other words to express habitual tendencies, such as {病気|びょうき}がち (sickly) and {怠|なま}けがち (tending to be lazy).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遠慮|えんりょ}がちな{態度|たいど} (a reserved attitude)
- {遠慮|えんりょ}がちな{性格|せいかく} (a diffident personality)
- {遠慮|えんりょ}がちに{話|はな}す (to speak hesitantly)
- {遠慮|えんりょ}がちに{笑|わら}う (to smile shyly)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {控|ひか}えめ: modest, restrained — suggests deliberate restraint, often seen as a positive trait
- {内気|うちき}: shy, introverted — describes an inherent personality trait rather than a behavioral tendency
